headline: US Personal Income Rose 0.7% in October 2026
summary: U.S. personal income increased by $201.8 billion, or 0.7%, in October, while personal consumption expenditures rose by 0.3%. Disposable personal income also saw a monthly gain of 0.8%.
why: Personal income and spending data are key indicators of consumer health, which accounts for the majority of U.S. economic activity and influences inflation trends.

impacts.name: S&P 500
impacts.why: Higher consumer spending supports corporate revenue growth, which is positive for equity markets.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Strong income and spending data suggest the consumer remains resilient, reducing recession fears and supporting market sentiment.
